The reset event is removed rather than placed. It is the one of the sixteen that is not a violating branch: the generated API 30 MessageDigest rule declares getInstance, update and digest and models no reset at all, so CogniCrypt ignores reset() calls entirely. The .mop event had an empty body -- it wrote no property, read none and reported nothing -- and was absent from the ere, so the whole of its effect was the all-fail row that turned a legitimate API call into a sequence violation and reset the monitor. Placing it would mean deciding, without the rule's support, where reset() belongs in the order; removing it restores the generated rule's behaviour exactly. MetaCrySL does model reset for the BouncyCastle digests, and there too it is declared in EVENTS and left out of the ORDER -- the same shape as this defect, one level up.
